K-T2: faults of the pictures (see T09.pictures.saved); each is also a row T09.warning.<name> and a warning in the runner's report.

expected: the linear depth texture of ReDefinitionAtmospheresLayerDepth.shader at a pixel on the terrain 500 m ahead equals the distance along the camera's axis within 5 percent. [VERIFY] that _CameraDepthTexture is readable at BeforeForwardAlpha under the Deferred mod (premise of the module). Probe pending.

brief acceptance: the deck's luminance at 10 km of air path follows the reference aerial-perspective curve (exp(-tau(lambda)) of the body's air times the unhazed deck plus the in-scatter share) within 15 percent. Reference: the analytic fog formula with the coefficients CloudBridgeAir.From gives for Kerbin, evaluated in numpy from the first-hit distance (the T06 haze.model_error method). Expected: passes, the shader evaluates the same formula (T06: 0.00045). Probe pending.
as above at 30 km. Expected: passes.

blue over red of the deck at 60 km against the reference curve, 15 percent. Expected: passes by construction of the formula; whether the strength is right in size against a real photograph is a taste item (T3).

brief acceptance 'no change without Scatterer': the haze term of the own pass (own coefficients, CloudBridgeAir) is the same with and without Scatterer in the mod set; the deck luminance at 30 km differs by at most 5 percent between the two mod sets once the sun colour is equal. Expected: the pass itself does not depend on Scatterer except for one switch (SunAirHeightM is zero with Scatterer loaded, tuning cloud.sunAirWithScatterer): so the delta is the sun colour's, not the haze's. Probe pending.

brief acceptance: the same pass under TUFX with a fixed exposure and with the auto exposure: the cloud over sky pixel ratio differs by at most 3 percent. Expected: passes, the clouds are written in scene radiance before the image effects, so the exposure scales both alike. Premise: the sun gain (tuning cloud.sunGain, 1) puts the cloud radiance in the sky's units; this row does not test it, T09.exposure.cloud_over_sky does. Probe pending.

calibration, not an acceptance: a lit cumulus flank over the sky next to it at noon, in the tone-mapped frame. The band is the owner-visible range for a cloud that reads as white against a blue sky; the unit of the sun colour (sun light colour times intensity times cloud.sunGain) is the first thing the first start settles. Expected: outside the band on the first start (the gain is a guess).

interaction row, fast flashes with DLSS (review T07-3): after a flash peak (cloud flash on, brightness 1, up to 3 strokes in a second) the residual of the flash in the frames 2 to 8 after it, measured as the C21 ghost ratio on the cloud pixels, stays at or under the C21 limit 0.012. Expected: passes, no DLSS history reset per flash was kept (dropped in the T07 fix) and the flash envelope (FlashEnvelope) falls within 150 ms; the hazard is the upscaler's history of a bright frame. If it fails the way back is a reset above a brightness-jump threshold with a switch (open-items-T-wave4). Probe pending.
the C21 trail limit 0.14 for the same flash sequence. Expected: passes.

with frame generation on (DLSS FG), a flash frame is never shown twice or replaced by an interpolated dark frame: duplicates in the FG replay over 30 s of flashes, 0. Expected: 0, the pass is part of the scene colour before the HUD-less copy (the statement in OwnCloudModule's header). Probe pending.
the HUD-less frame of frame generation carries the flash like the full frame (mean absolute difference of the cloud pixels, 1 percent). Expected: passes.
the photosensitivity limit stays 3 in the integrated frame (T07 row, repeated with the module running). Expected: 3 or fewer.

interaction row, the descent through 200 to 260 km with the 2D shell and the near march both on (review T06-1): coverage over the cloud pixels per km of altitude across the blend. Expected: passes, the shell fades with OwnShell.Opacity (1 - NearWeight) while the near march is drawing (NearMarchActive is set by the module), and the T06 sweep alone gave 4e-6 per km. Probe pending: the descent is a scripted vessel placement at 270, 260, 250, 240, 230, 220, 210, 200 km, 20 s each.

luminance over the cloud pixels per km across the blend, same descent. Expected: the T06 gate 'luminance within 5 percent' was open (far against dense march 7.4 percent): expect up to 0.074 per step at the band edges; this row may fail and is then the measured size of the open defect.
the shell's luminance against the near march's at the altitude where both are drawn with equal weight, 5 percent (T06 brief gate). Expected: fails near 0.074 (open since T06).

the blended picture's cloud luminance over the near march alone at the same pose: at most 1.02, i.e. no brightening from drawing both. Expected: passes (the shell's weight is 1 - w, the march's picture is not weighted: the sum is alpha-composited, so a deck is slightly brighter where the shell is still on; if above 1.02 the shell's weight needs the march's alpha in it).
at and below 200 km the shell's opacity is 0 while the own pass draws (OwnShell.Opacity with NearMarchActive true); above 260 km the pass fades by the policy. Expected: 1.

interaction row (review T06-5, the in-scatter must follow the sky): the haze colour's luminance of the far deck at night (sun 20 degrees below the horizon, moons per the moon source) over the same at noon. CloudBridgeAir.Inscatter gives sun-term x 0.23 with the ambient as a floor, so at night it is the scene's ambient light: expected 0.01 to 0.05 depending on the ambient KSP sets. A day-coloured haze at night would be 1.

the haze's red over blue at sunset (sun 2 degrees) divided by the same at noon: at least 1.5. Expected: passes if the sun light colour KSP sets reddens at sunset (stock does not; Scatterer's does): without Scatterer this row is expected to FAIL at about 1.0, which is the measured size of 'the sun colour in the game does not carry the air path'. The cloud light itself reddens through SunAirHeightM; the haze takes the colour it is given.

the far end of the deck converges to the colour of the sky at the horizon next to it: relative colour distance at most 25 percent at noon and at sunset. Expected: noon passes near 0.2; sunset is the taste item (the Scatterer sky is Scatterer's, ours is a model).

at night with a moon above the horizon the moon light reaches the pass (CloudBridgeLights.Moon assigned by the main mod; OwnCloudModule fills Lights[0]). Expected: 1; the main mod fills HostSeams.CloudMoonLight in HostLink.Fill (RtReflectors.CloudLight at the nightClouds percentage) and CloudBridgeLights.Moon reads it. Probe pending.

the GPU profiler's report holds the segment between the labels 'ReDefinition clouds: begin' and 'ReDefinition clouds: end' while the own pass draws (HostSeams.GpuMark = GpuProfiler.Mark, CloudBridgeLights.Mark); kt2.py reads the T09.perf rows from it. Expected: 1 with -redefinitionGpuProfile; without the profiler's plugin the marks are no-ops. Probe pending.

the sun-lit luminance of terrain under a dense deck over the same terrain in the clear (cloudShadows on against off, same pose): at most 0.6 under a cumulonimbus. [VERIFY under the Deferred mod that the multiply at AfterScreenspaceMask reaches the lit picture.] Probe pending.

Probe pending; belongs to T08, carried in the first integrated series as the review demanded.

the depth-aware composite does not paint cloud over terrain nearer than the cloud (mountains in front of a deck at 10 km): the fraction of terrain pixels with cloud alpha above 0.05 where the scene depth is less than the cloud's first hit, at most 2 percent. Expected: passes if the depth premise holds; failing means the cloud sits on the wrong camera (Camera 00 against the far camera) or reads no depth.
raytracing on adds at most 0.5 ms to the cloud pass itself (the rays do not read the layers: RtOwnClouds is not delivered, so the delta is zero by construction). Expected: ~0.

the ratio of the sums over the views of the own plain pass's cost over TVC's cost (cost = frame minus off frame, each; a mean of per-view ratios would be dominated by the view with the smallest denominator). the label measure of the own pass (the profiler's group 'ReDefinition clouds': both markers) against the frame difference, the largest relative gap over the own views whose cost is above 0.5 ms and that are not cpu-bound (GPU idle share under 10 percent; the frame difference hides the cost of a cpu-bound view). Not a default decision: the reconstruction stays off until the owner decides, and T14 turns it into a slider.

the worst height-map build after the first, from its start to its finished maps, ON THE WORKER (HeightJob; the first call is emitted apart as T09.height_build_first_ms): four layers at 512x256 every 20 s. Not a frame cost: start 42 measured 440 to 519 ms for it on the main thread, which is why it moved. Expected: 100 to 400 ms (the noise of the layers is cached after the first build); the limit only catches a build that hangs. The main thread's share is T09.height_build_main_ms.

the worst single frame the main thread spends on the height build: starting it (the plan, copies of the tunings), the budgeted reading of a field that is not thread safe (0.8 ms), taking a finished result and giving the stack its maps; the first call (Mono's JIT) is left out. Expected: 0.1 to 1 ms (the game's field is thread safe, so the reading is on the worker).

the worst frame of LayerRenderer.Upload plus the height slice written that frame (HeightMapStore.Step: a copy of one 512x256 slice prepared on the worker, SetPixelData; the array is applied once, with the last slice), after the first frame. Start 42 measured 4.66 ms with the slice converted on the main thread. Expected: 0.3 to 1.5 ms; a stack upload with its profile tables is in the same figure.

INFORMATIONAL (no limit: any hitch lands in a sum of steps; the required row is T09.map_fetch_main_ms, one frame's cost). The worst map fetch round after the first, summed over its steps (coverage, precipitation and a layer coverage for each layer, each packed to bytes once; one step a frame, once a second). A round for a new stack runs in one frame and is left out. Start 42 measured 5.5 ms typical and 45.3 ms once with the whole round in one frame. The cost of one frame is T09.map_fetch_main_ms.

the worst single frame the main thread spends on a step of the map fetch (one map copied from the field and packed to bytes, 0.5 MB), rounds for a new stack and the first round left out. Expected: 0.3 to 1.5 ms.

how often the pass's command buffers were put on the camera in a variant (they are added once and stay; once a second the camera is asked whether they are still there). Expected: 1 to 3; a count in the hundreds would mean they are re-added every frame (cloud.readdEveryFrame) or lost.

Expected 0.6 to 0.72; the limits 0.5 to 0.8 are those of the field's cover being a covered sky that is not a closed deck.

the sun's elevation over the site at the chosen time: the narrow band 30 to 55 degrees of K-T2d (start 45: 45.5, the light the pass was measured at: frameSun luminance 1.90, warm colour (2.12, 1.88, 1.47)). A start that fell back to the wide band 15 to 60 reads T09.sun_band_narrow 0 and may fail this row: a sun at 15 degrees is the start 44 light (luminance 0.415), not comparable.

NOISE, written before the run. Flicker = the mean absolute difference of luminance between two frames of the held pose, one frame apart, over the pixels the pass changed (ground and above views; mean of the two views' ratios to plain). The player measured the shimmer falling 5 to 10 times with levels 2 to 4 (T14; T05's static ground shimmer at level 4 was 0.0006 of the display value against the 0.0015 limit). Expected for level 2: 0.1 to 0.3 (a fall of 3 to 10 times); the limits 0.05 to 0.5 mean at least a halving and no collapse (below 0.05 the history would be frozen, a smear).
level 3: expected 0.1 to 0.25, and not above level 2's by more than 0.05.
level 4: expected 0.1 to 0.2 (the 5 to 10 times fall of the player), and below level 3's.

NOISE, informational (no limit): the spatial grain (RMS of the 4-neighbour high-pass over the interior of the changed region) of level 2 over plain. The reconstruction accumulates samples over the block cycle, so the grain falls with the level; expected 0.1 to 0.6. A value above 1 would mean the reconstruction adds grain (block pattern).
level 3, informational: expected 0.1 to 0.5.

cloud.moonGain 2 doubles the moon light the pass receives (Lights[0] colour). Only where a moon or planet lights the clouds at the chosen time and cloudMoonLights lets it through; otherwise the probe emits T09.gain.moon_note and this row is SKIP: the key has no effect in the day.

K-T2d (the diagnosis of the black own clouds, tests/series/K-T2d.json): the field's cover at 3 km at the universal time of the 'low' runs (the clock step picks the candidate hour nearest 0.3 whose sun stands 15 to 60 degrees up). Outside the band means no hour in the band had the sun in the band (T09d.cover_off_band is then 1) and the low runs are not about 0.3. T09.cover.<ut> lists the cover of all 48 candidate hours.
the same for the 'high' runs (about 0.7).

the baseline: the sky above the horizon of the ground view at the high cover, the pass running with no layer drawn, raw values of the camera target (no gamma step), median of the region. Start 42 (cover 0.514): 0.31 / 0.49 / 0.69 over three heights of the sky. Everything below is read against this and against the sunlit sea.

the sunlit sea or ground below the horizon of the ground view, baseline frame: the white reference in the target's units (start 42's sea from above: 0.53 / 0.72 / 0.92). deck_over_off_ground in the rows below divides by this.

EXPECTED (written before the run, tests/series/K-T2d.json description has the table). The deck (the pixels the pass changed against the baseline) at cloud.sunGain 1. Start 42 measured the ground sky at median 0.020 (p90 0.063); the offline raw value (Player, sun 0.844 to 1.0) is 0.063 to 0.083. Prediction A (units/composition: nothing after the pass clamps): 0.02 to 0.08. Both predictions agree at gain 1, the gains below separate them.
gain 4. A: 4 times the gain-1 value (0.08 to 0.32). B (something after the pass clamps or darkens): less than twice the gain-1 value, or the same value.

gain 16. A: 16 times the gain-1 value (0.32 to 1.3), clipped at 1.0 where the target is not HDR (deck_clipped says so; start 42's offline raw 0.075 x 16 = 1.2). B: stays at the value of gain 4, or saturates at a constant below 1.

the linearity test, no constant fit: deck median at gain 4 over gain 1. A: 3.2 to 4.4 (the sky behind the deck is gone, alpha 1, so the deck is the pass's radiance alone). Under 3.0 is prediction B (clamped or darkened after the pass, or the composition is not rgb + dst x (1 - alpha)).
A: 16 until the clip (smaller by the clip: 1.0 over the gain-1 value). B: near the gain-4 ratio.

the deck at gain 1 over the baseline sky, units free. Start 42: 0.02 / 0.49 = 0.04 (offline raw 0.075 / 0.49 = 0.15). The reciprocal is the missing factor of the sun's unit against the sky's, and 1 / this value is the gain at which the deck reaches the sky under prediction A (6 to 25).
gain 16. A: 0.6 to 1 and above (units: the deck reaches the sky's level somewhere between gain 6 and 25). B: under 0.2.

the deck over the baseline sunlit sea (the white reference in the same units): the ratio of the cloud to a surface lit by the sun, read without a constant. Offline: the deck underside of a thick deck is 0.1 to 0.2 of a sunlit white surface; start 42 measured about 0.03 (0.02 / 0.72).

the share of the picture's samples the pass changed (the vessel box and the top and bottom edge left out). Start 42: the whole sky above the horizon (about 0.8 of the picture). At about 0.7 expect 0.7 to 0.95 (the layer threshold 0.5, edge 0.2).

the same at the cover of about 0.3: the layer shape saturate((map + noise + coverage - 1) / edge + 0.5) with coverage 0.5 and a map value of 0.3 leaves a broken deck, or none (deck_n 0 and no deck rows is a legitimate result). If a deck exists its median should read like the high cover's (a thick patch is thick whatever the share of sky): the point of the second cover is the deck fraction, not the value.
expected 0 to 0.5 at the cover of about 0.3. Start 42 had only covers of 0.514 and up, so there was never a clear sky to see.
the sky region of the plain frame over the baseline sky: 1.0 where the pass left the sky alone, below 1 where the deck covers most of the region (it is the median of the region).

the sea below the horizon of the ground view is not touched by the pass (start 42: the sea was untouched): 1.0. A value far from 1 means the pass writes over the sea too, or the baseline and the plain frames differ in the sun (the clouds' shadow is not drawn by the pass).
the view above the layers looking down: the sky above the horizon of the baseline frame.
the sunlit sea or ground under the deck, baseline frame: the white reference of this view (start 42: 0.53 / 0.72 / 0.92).
the deck seen from above at gain 1. Start 42: cloud areas 0.118 next to a sunlit sea at 0.72; offline raw 0.19 to 0.20 at sun luminance 1 (0.17 at 0.844). A: 0.1 to 0.2.
A: 4 times gain 1 (0.4 to 0.8), before the clip; B: below twice.
A: clipped at 1.0 (16 x 0.12 = 1.9). B: the same constant as gain 4.

the deck from above over the baseline sunlit sea. Start 42: 0.118 / 0.72 = 0.16. A white surface is 1.0; a thick cloud top in the same units is 0.8 to 1.0, so the factor the sun's unit is short by is 5 to 6 here (about 1 / 0.16).
A: 1 or more (clipped at 1 / sea). B: under 0.3.
the share of the deck samples with a channel at 0.999 or more: 0 at gain 1 in both predictions.

aid 4 over the natural frame's deck: r is the pass's direct light (luminance), g the light taps, b the ambient (luminance), alpha as drawn. Compared with the natural deck_median at gain 1 (0.02 to 0.08): if the direct light is of the order of the sun colour (0.84 at gain 1, times the transmittance to the point) while the deck is 0.02, the loss is in what the pass does with the light (phase, extinction, albedo) or after it; if direct is itself 0.02 to 0.1, the light the pass is given is the problem.

the ambient the pass used under the deck (start 42's log: not logged; the pass floors the deck's light at 3 percent of the sun's luminance). Read with the environment lines T09d env frameAmbient and renderSettingsAmbient.
